captured_note: Ported from the capture's self-contained methods/3_colorization, specifically its paper-faithful CNN path (models/colorization_cnn.py, data/colorization_dataset.py, data/ab_quantization.py, train_pretrain_cnn.py, evaluate_linear.py). These are the lab's own implementation of Zhang, Isola & Efros (ECCV 2016) colorization. The capture directory number (3) equals this method's number in the Step 1&2 list (see docs/PORTING_ROADMAP.md).
scope: The paper-faithful CNN path is ported: the L channel of a Lab image is the input, and a VGG-style CNN with BatchNorm and dilated convolutions predicts the ab channels, quantised to 313 in-gamut bins, as a per-pixel classification trained with an (optionally class-rebalanced) cross-entropy. The capture's unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (models/vit_colorization.py, arch: vit) is also ported additively: a from-scratch ViT-B/16 (hand-written attention -- no timm) reads the L channel (in_chans=1) and a lightweight CNN decoder upsamples the patch grid back to the same 313-bin per-pixel ab classification, AdamW + warmup/cosine + AMP + grad-clip, milestone checkpoints; the native CNN path is byte-for-byte unchanged, and because the ViT is self-contained the closure stays torch-only.
encoder: encoder.pt is the encoder trunk (encoder.*): the CNN trunk (conv1-7) natively, or the from-scratch ViT trunk (patch embed, CLS, position embedding, blocks, norm) on arch: vit. The decoder and the 313-bin classification head are pretext machinery and are excluded from both. The CNN's flat layer names (conv1_1 ... conv_out) are grouped into encoder/decoder/head so encoder.pt is a clean encoder.* prefix; the ViT trunk lives under self.encoder for the same reason. get_encoder() returns the CNN trunk with a global-average-pool -> 512-d, or the ViT CLS embedding (embed_dim); the eval calls it, so either arch probes correctly.
linear_eval: Reads the trained encoder.pt and probes the encoder's 512-d global-average-pooled feature (the frozen encoder reads the L channel), a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable. Follows the lab's shared ARSSL probe (mean-centre + L2-normalise, single linear layer, SGD momentum + cosine, top1/top5) rather than the capture's own per-layer probe, so the number is comparable across the ported methods.

vendored_constant.note: The 313 in-gamut ab-bin centres (Zhang et al.). The capture's copy is a symlink into the cluster's LIVE_ROOT (not in the snapshot), so the port vendors the authoritative constant fetched once from richzhang/colorization; there is no runtime download.

rewritten_during_the_port: the unified ViT-B/16 Step 2 (arch: vit) is ported additively (models/vit_colorization.py, train_pretrain_vit_colorization.py, configs/pretrain_vit.yaml), port-authored from the capture's models/colorization_vit.py + train_step2_vit.py; it is a from-scratch, hand-written ViT-B/16 (no timm) reading the L channel + a CNN decoder for the same 313-bin ab classification, reusing the port's ColorizationDataset/get_class_weights and resolve_device/make_deterministic. The ViT trunk's position embedding is sized to the crop (the actual input), not the resize img_size. Being self-contained, it adds no dependency -- the closure stays torch-only

the model's flat layer names (conv1_1 ... conv_out) are grouped into encoder (conv1-7) / decoder (conv8) / head (313-bin 1x1), so encoder.pt is a clean encoder.* prefix; the layer shapes, order and computation are unchanged

the RGB->CIE Lab conversion and the 313-bin ab quantisation are pure numpy (as in the lab's own code); despite the capture's requirements.txt naming opencv / scikit-image / scikit-learn, none is imported, so the port keeps the torch-only closure
the 313 ab-bin constant is vendored (the capture's copy is a symlink into the cluster's LIVE_ROOT); the runtime download / approximate-fallback paths are removed -- a missing constant errors loudly
class rebalancing is exposed as a config flag (use_class_rebalancing); the shipped config enables it, the hermetic smoke disables it
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
main() split into build_parser()/run(args, config) returning the pretext cross-entropy loss and epoch count
the run is seeded through make_deterministic (python, numpy, torch)
the training loop drops the upstream DistributedDataParallel, AMP and TensorBoard so the same step runs on a CPU or a GPU unchanged, single-process fp32
DATA_ROOT is the dataset root; the pretrain stage reads its train/ subdirectory (unified data-root convention via adapterlib.dataset_split_dir).
